title: Complete bathroom practical and inspection
moduleTitle: Group (Cleaning & Hygiene): Quality, evidence and handover
audience: Cleaners completing the end-to-end bathroom practical and inspection.
learningOutcomes: Explain the hazards, boundaries and quality standards for an end-to-end bathroom service.
Complete the bathroom practical and inspection using authorised methods.
Record results and escalate unsafe or out-of-scope conditions.

instruction.heading: Context and safety boundaries
instruction.body: A two-bathroom property must be cleaned to an agreed checklist while occupants are present. Translate the work order into a timed sequence, the contamination zones, and the quality acceptance criteria before you start. Follow the site-specific procedures, the current product labels and supervision. Stop if the task becomes unsafe or falls outside your authorisation.

instruction.heading: Preparation and method
instruction.body: Carry out a pre-start risk check. Stage clean and sanitary tools separately, and keep the toilet tools apart from the basin tools. Clean the high and low contact points in an orderly sequence, manage the waste, and change cloths at the right points. Inspect mirrors, taps, shower tracks, toilets and floors against the checklist, correct defects, record exceptions, and hand over without exposing private details.

instruction.heading: Reasoned workplace decision
instruction.body: During the practical, the assessor places a toilet brush in the basin. Stop the task, isolate the affected tools and surfaces, and demonstrate recovery: remove the item from use, re-clean the surface with clean tools and the approved product, and record the event.

instruction.heading: Quality standards and records
instruction.body: The assessor checks hazard control, hygiene segregation, finish protection, inspection accuracy, correction and handover. Record the product used where required, the exceptions, the corrective actions and the final supervisor sign-off. Completion means observable safe work and verified quality, not a ticked checklist.

instruction.heading: Transfer to the workplace
instruction.body: Before using this method at a real site, compare the practice setting with the actual surfaces, occupants, chemical instructions, equipment condition and scope. Where any assumption differs, reassess the risk and obtain approval before continuing.

procedure: Translate the work order into a timed sequence, zones and acceptance criteria.
Carry out the pre-start risk check and stage tools by zone.
Clean high and low contact points in order, managing waste and cloth changes.
Inspect against the checklist, correct defects, and record exceptions.
Hand over with a privacy-safe record and the supervisor sign-off.

workedExamples.situation: A two-bathroom property must be cleaned to an agreed checklist while occupants are present.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do first, which hazard or boundary could require stopping, and how do you verify completion?
workedExamples.reasoning: First confirm scope, occupants and the hazard scan, and set out zones and tools. Stop if a hazard is found outside authorisation, or if occupants or sharps create a risk. Verify completion by the inspection route and the checklist, with the record and the sign-off.

equipmentAndPpe: Zone-coded cloths and tools, as set by the site procedure.
Approved bathroom products with labels and SDS available.
Gloves and eye protection as set by the SDS.

commonErrors.error: Using toilet tools in the basin.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep zone-coded tools apart and recover by re-cleaning.

commonErrors.error: Ticking the checklist before the inspection.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect first, then complete the checklist.

commonErrors.error: Mixing products to speed up the work.
commonErrors.prevention: Use one approved product at a time.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Chemicals must be managed under the label, the SDS and, where kept, the hazardous chemicals register.
Unauthorised electrical or gas work is outside this practical. This practical does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Pre-start risk check completed before the practical.
Stop-work decision and recovery demonstrated when a critical error is introduced.
Inspection passed against the checklist, with defects corrected and recorded.
documentationEvidence: Completed pre-start hazard and scope check.
Assessor observation against the critical steps.
summary: Plan the timed sequence, zones and acceptance criteria first.
Stop and recover from critical errors, then continue.
Inspect against the checklist and correct defects.
Record and hand over with supervisor sign-off.

knowledgeChecks.question: During a practical, a toilet brush is found in the basin. What is the correct response?
options: Finish the basin first, then note the brush for the next training session
Rinse the brush and return it to the same toilet tool set
Stop, isolate the affected tools and surfaces, and recover by re-cleaning

knowledgeChecks.question: What does completion of this practical mean?
options: Observable safe work and verified quality, recorded
The checklist is ticked and the form is signed off
The learner has a licence to work unsupervised

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a pre-start risk check done before the practical?
options: To use up the time left in the session before work
To confirm scope and hazards before choosing a method
Because the checklist requires it after the clean

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the quality standards and records section say the record of the practical includes?
options: The product used where required, the exceptions, the corrective actions and the final supervisor sign-off
